messages:
maya: Heads-up — the eval CI hung on the quantized bring-up canary (job: eval/quant-canary-2309). Runner pod stayed Running but test never progressed past 'prepare-batches'.
sanjay: ack. which model and which runner image?
maya: llama3c-q8 on runner:v0.42.3, node k8s-ml-5. CI link: https://ci.redwood.internal/2309
ci-bot: build 2309 started by maya — https://ci.redwood.internal/2309 
liam: grabbing logs now. `kubectl logs -n eval runner-quant-2309 -c executor`
liam: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-19T14:12:02Z] runner: executor:0 waiting for task forever
[2026-03-19T14:12:10Z] batcher: no work, sleeping
[2026-03-19T14:12:15Z] runtime: kernel fallback -> q8_generic
[2026-03-19T14:12:20Z] cgroup: cpu throttled for 100ms
[2026-03-19T14:12:45Z] executor:0 still waiting, heartbeat ok
```
eva: hm cgroup throttling + executor stuck looks like host-level CPU contention or docker/cgroup config change. Any recent infra changes?
maya: infra-team rolled docker engine to 20.10.18 on that pool yesterday (PR infra/337). Also noticed a kubelet flag change on that node: --cpu-cfs-quota=true toggled.
dmitri: that kubelet flag can make bursty inference work worse if quotas are strict. We've seen long-tail waits on pinned threads before.
sanjay: quick repro: run the harness shell on the same node, run `stress-ng --cpu 4 --timeout 30s` while starting the runner image, see if the executor starves.
liam: reproduced locally — heavy CPU load + cfs quota => executor queue grows and batcher stalls.
ci-bot: note — affected jobs: eval/quant-canary-2309, eval/quant-canary-2310, nightly/eval-quant-llama3c.
maya: bisect plan: 1) rerun job on nodes with cpu-cfs-quota=false 2) rollback runtime to v0.42.2 3) pin node to older docker engine. Any objections?
eva: agree with order 1 then 2. rollback runtime may mask root cause if it's infra.
dmitri: we should also capture `docker stats` and `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us` when it stalls. Add a tiny cron to collect those metrics during job window.
liam: ran the job on a node with cpu-cfs-quota=false — job completed, metrics look normal.
sanjay: runtime rollback to v0.42.2 on a fresh node also passes, but that runtime has different thread-pool defaults (smaller affinity changes).
maya: so both infra flag and runtime change correlate. Root cause likely interaction: newer runtime increased per-executor CPU burstiness and kubelet quota now enforces limits, causing stall.
eva: mitigation path: revert kubelet flag on canary nodes and update runner to include backpressure (PR #2419 suggested earlier) — but PR #2419 changed thread affinity and was merged last week.
dmitri: suggestion: revert PR #2419 in runtime for canary channel, and open an infra rollback for kubelet flag on the affected pool. Do both with canary first.
maya: action items:
- maya: open rollback PR for infra (kubelet flag) and target canary pool (infra/341)
- liam: revert runtime PR #2419 on canary runtime branch and trigger canary builds
- sanjay: add cgroup diagnostic collector to eval job (script + docker stats)
- eva: run canary jobs and confirm stability by EOD
All: please react with :eyes: when you've picked up an item.
liam: picked up runtime revert. :thumbsup:
sanjay: added diagnostic script in eval job config, pushed branch eval/diag-cgroups.
ci-bot: runtime-canary build 2311 triggered by liam — https://ci.redwood.internal/2311
maya: after infra rollback on k8s-ml-5 and runtime revert, canary passed twice in a row, no more cgroup throttles in logs.
eva: leaving note for release: quantify impact and add a checklist item for cgroup behaviour on future runtime upgrades. Also add an automated test that stresses CPU with quotas on PRs that touch thread scheduling.
maya: thanks everyone — closing thread once postmortem doc is up (will add link).
